newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- LATE RECOVERY, BUT STILL WEAKER.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- LATE RECOVERY, BUT STILL WEAKER.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices staged a modest comeback Monday in quiet afternoon action, but finished the day slightly lower nonetheless.
Traders said quotes were unchanged to down 1/8, but very few bonds were changing hands. Earlier in the day, prices were off as much as 1/4 point.

The muni market's trend followed Treasuries throughout the day. Following early losses, the government market moved into positive territory in the afternoon when Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips suggested an immediate interest rate rise might not be needed.
The government long bond was up 3/32 to 96-23/32, pushing the yield down to 6.63 percent.

Futures prices also returned to nearly unchanged at the close. September municipals ended up 1/32 to 118-30/32, while September T-bonds gained 2/32 to 112-24/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 198 ticks from 199 at the close on Friday.
Muni market players said the large new issue calendar and several key July economic data releases this week continue to be the focus.
On Wednesday, the market receives two important numbers, retail sales and the producer price index report.

Economists polled by Reuters expect a 0.7 percent rise in retail sales overall, and a 0.5 percent sales gain excluding autos. Wednesday's PPI report is expected to show a O.1 percent rise both overall and in the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices.
The July consumer price index is set for release Thursday. CPI is expected to rise 0.2 percent both overall and in the core rate.

In muni secondary action, bids on Dade County, Fla., FGIC water and sewer 5-1/4s of 2026 were up one basis point to 5.54 percent. Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 5.0s of 2024 were one basis points lower, at 5.55 percent.
Municipal bond sales for Tuesday were expected to total $2.1 billion in 45 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totalled $1.4 billion in 16 sales, with a $446 million New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority offering through Smith Barney Inc topping the list.
